evidence.source: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.field: 漢字甲骨部件分析; character 人; shape and gloss
evidence.text: The database describes ancient 人 as a profile figure standing with arms lowered and gives ‘person’ as its original sense. It reports oracle-bone examples 《合集》22626 ‘伐十人’ and 《合集》20328 ‘余一人’. These are cited corpus references, but this page does not date the individual specimens.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 漢字甲骨部件分析: 人

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Institute of History and Philology, Chinese Character Database
evidence.text: The entry lists oracle-bone form 合集6175, bronze form 集成00944, and Small Seal / Shuowen material. Its account reads the graph as a person standing in profile: head, body, an extended stroke as arm, and legs. This is the database’s graphic interpretation; it does not date those specimens or establish a stroke-by-stroke chronology.
evidence.title: 漢字「人」：字形演變

evidence.source: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.field: 甲骨文用法; 通假 and bronze use
evidence.text: The database reports 人 used for the state name 夷 in oracle-bone phrase 人方, and 人 used for 年 in bronze inscription 甫人父匜 (‘萬人用’, interpreted as ‘萬年用’). It separately describes 人 as the phonetic element in 年. These are source assertions about whole-graph loans/usages; the page does not independently establish their sound correspondences.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 漢字甲骨部件分析: 人

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 研訂瀏覽; historical-form claims and Mandarin reading
evidence.text: The entry quotes Shuowen’s explanation that 人 depicts arm and shin forms. It cautions that certain ancient forms reported in later references are not found in oracle-bone, bronze, or ancient Zhou-script materials, and says their evidence is unknown. It records modern Mandarin rén. This cautions against treating unsupported later-reported shapes as ancestors, but does not dispute the profile-person interpretation.

search_audit.outcome: Found and inspected the exact 人-oracle.svg page; it identifies the Shang oracle-style redraw, specimen reference, original file link, and CC0 status. The SVG fetch itself failed due to unsupported content type. Other result pages were inspected as candidates but not selected.

gaps: No individual date was found for cited oracle-bone specimen references; the sources classify them as oracle-bone material but do not supply a character-specific first-use date.

The sources identify the original sense as ‘person’ and provide Shang oracle-bone instances, then list later bronze and textual uses such as common people, people/population, and ruler’s self-reference. They do not provide a complete dated semantic chronology or prove every link between these uses.

The reported whole-graph loans 人-for-夷 and 人-for-年 are not independently phonologically established in the inspected evidence. The separate statement that 人 functions as 年’s phonetic element does not itself establish the sound basis for the whole-graph loan.

Shuowen’s explanation is preserved as a historical account, not independent proof. The inspected paleographic descriptions support a human profile interpretation; the Taiwan MOE entry warns that some forms later labelled ancient lack attestation in early corpora.

The character-specific Unicode Unihan endpoint failed to load. The local kMandarin and Baxter–Sagart rows remain local metadata; current reading metadata is not evidence of ancient sound relationships.
The selected historical glyphs are modern vector redrawings. The web tool could not fetch their SVG pixels, so no visual inspection is claimed.
